# Report Conventions

Defines the HTML report structure, styling, and behavior. Referenced by `azea-report`.

---

## Overview

The assessment report is a **self-contained HTML dashboard** — a single `.html` file with all CSS and JavaScript inline. No external dependencies. It should open in any browser and be shareable via email.

Use `samples/sample-report.html` as the **exact template** for styling and structure.

## File Naming

- Single assessment: `assessment-{subscription-name}-{YYYY-MM-DD}.html`
- Same-day repeat: `assessment-{subscription-name}-{YYYY-MM-DD}-{HHMMSS}.html`
- Baselines: `baselines/baseline-{subscription-name}-{YYYY-MM-DD}.json`

## Report Sections

### Header
- Title: "Azure Environment Assessment"
- Subtitle: subscription name and ID
- Meta: date, profile (startup/scale-up/enterprise with estimated team size), primary region, total resources scanned

### Summary Cards
Count of findings by severity: Critical, High, Medium, Low, Passed. Color-coded using the project color scheme (see `severity-calculation.md`).

### Pillar Score Cards
- One card per pillar (Security, Reliability, Cost, Operations, Performance, Governance)
- SVG circular progress indicator showing percentage score
- Pillar icon, name, and finding count breakdown
- Color based on score level (see `severity-calculation.md`)

### Filter Bar
- Severity filter buttons: All, Critical, High, Medium, Low
- Pillar filter buttons: All, then one per pillar with icon
- Filters work in combination (severity AND pillar)
- Active filter gets blue highlight (`#0078d4`)

### Findings List
- Each finding is a collapsible card
- Every finding `<div>` MUST include `data-severity` and `data-pillar` attributes for filtering
- **Header** (always visible): severity badge, rule ID + title, affected resource, pillar tag, expand chevron
- **Body** (expands on click): What was found, Why it matters, Recommendation, Learn More links
- First critical finding expanded by default (class `open`). If no Critical, expand first High. If no High, expand first finding.
- Sort: Critical → High → Medium → Low

### Passed Checks
Collapsible summary after findings list showing what's working well.

### Remediation Actions (Optional)
If the `azea-remediate` skill was used, include a remediation summary section after the findings list:
- **Remediated findings** — findings that were fixed via ARM template deployment, with deployment status
- **Pending findings** — findings that can be remediated but were not yet addressed
- Each remediated finding card shows a "✅ Remediated" badge with the deployment timestamp

Individual finding cards may include a remediation status indicator:
- `data-remediated="true"` attribute on remediated finding `<div>` elements
- Remediated findings show a green "Remediated" badge next to the severity badge
- Filter bar includes a "Remediated" toggle to show/hide fixed findings

### Footer
- "Generated by Azure Environment Advisor" with GitHub repo link
- Framework references: WAF, CAF, ALZ
- "Point-in-time assessment" reminder
- Assessment Limitations (if any): rules that could not be evaluated and why

## JavaScript Functions

```javascript
toggleFinding(header)       // Toggle the 'open' class on finding click
filterFindings(severity, btn) // Filter by severity, update active button
filterPillar(pillar, btn)    // Filter by pillar, update active button
```

Combined filtering: both severity AND pillar must match.

## Print Styles

- Hide filters and chevrons
- Show all finding bodies expanded
- White background
- `break-inside: avoid` on findings

## Tone Guidelines

- Professional and constructive — this is an advisor, not an auditor
- Acknowledge what's done well (passed checks count)
- Frame recommendations as improvements, not criticisms
- Be specific: "Deploy a Private Endpoint for sql-contoso-prod" not "Consider using Private Endpoints"

## Microsoft Learn Links

- Only include links you are confident exist
- Format: `https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/{service}/{article}`
- Each finding should have 1–3 relevant links
- Links should point to remediation guidance, not just overview pages
